definitions.explanation: The degree to which two people, things, or elements go well together. Can refer to interpersonal chemistry, food pairings, or how well software or hardware works together.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{相性|あいしょう}がいい。
examples.english: The two of them are compatible.

examples.japanese: ワインとチーズは{相性|あいしょう}が{抜群|ばつぐん}だ。
examples.english: Wine and cheese go perfectly together.

examples.japanese: このソフトウェアは{古|ふる}いパソコンとの{相性|あいしょう}が{悪|わる}くて、よくフリーズする。
examples.english: This software has poor compatibility with old computers and freezes often.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used with がいい (good compatibility) or が{悪|わる}い (poor compatibility). Also common with {抜群|ばつぐん} (outstanding) and {最悪|さいあく} (worst). Used broadly — for people, food pairings, technology, and more.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {相性|あいしょう}がいい: compatible, go well together
- {相性|あいしょう}が{悪|わる}い: incompatible
- {相性|あいしょう}が{抜群|ばつぐん}: perfectly suited
- {相性|あいしょう}{診断|しんだん}: compatibility test
- ～との{相性|あいしょう}: compatibility with ~

HOMOPHONE:
- {愛称|あいしょう}: nickname, pet name (different meaning)
